We acknowledge your letter of 13th instant and regret incon- 
venience caused by the Schuller party by s/s "Taisang" last trip. 


As you are doubtless aware the local Government recently de- 
creed that all Aliens were to quit the Colony and to assist our Authori- 
ties, we agreed to accept a limited number provided their Bona Fides 
were guaranteed. 


The S.M.C. regulations of 22/10/39 were not overlooked but our 
Authorities who also are aware of these, assured us the requirements of 
the rules would be observed as regards any Aliens sent to your port. 


The "Schuller" party are not Jewish, or in the strict sense 
Refugees, having business connections at Shanghai. They were permitted 
to remain here under local guarantees, after the outbreak of hostiltties 
but with the tighening of restrictions the Authorities considered it

baggage etc.

accommodate the "Schuller" party as apparently stated by the Purser.

s/s "TAISANG” which arrived here on 10th June brought

The Shanghai Municipal Folice have now queried our 
carriage of these passengers in view of the regulations in 
force against the admission of refugees from kurope into 
Shanghai, which regulations were passed on to you in our 
letter of 26/12/39. We have explained to them that as we 
are informed by the Purser these passages were arranged by 
the Hongkong Government, other passengers having to be 
cancelled to accommodate them and that they were escorted 
on board by the Police. 


The Folice here fully appreciate that you had very 
little option in the matter but are still worried over the 
fact that the lack of any inspection of landing here deprives 
them of any opportunity of checking up whether such passengers 
are undesirable or otherwise. We have suggested that any 
action to prevent the carriage of such passengers rather lies 
out of our hands and could only be taken officially. They 
have promised to look into the matter and see whether they 
can make any effective communication to the Hongkong Government. 


It would be of considerable assistance to them, 
however, if they could have advance information of any similar 
passengers coming up by our steamers, and we suggest that in 
order to avoid further queries and possible complications you 


might include in your despatch wire to us brief mention of 80 
many Germans or so many Italians.

Subject Central European Jews ex Hongkong.
Made by D.S.I. Pitts. Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached communication
dated June 25, 1940 from Messrs. Indo-China Steam
Navigation Co. Ltd., regarding the entrance into
Shanghai of European refugees from Hongkong, it has
to be pointed out that in accordance with the
revised regulations effective as from July 1, 1940
"....no entry will be permitted unless an entry
permit has been obtained from the Police of the
International Settlement...."
Article (4) of the regulations stipulates that
the responsibility of verifying that an entry permit
has been issued by the Police before a passage
booking is made, devolves upon the shipping agents
concerned.
With these rules in mind, the tasks of Messrs.
Indo-China Steam Navigation Co. Lts. should be
considerably facilitated, since no refugee can now
land here without being in possession of a permit.
Since this office is greatly interested in
refugees and since all intending immigrants must be
in possession of permits, it would seem that the
shipping company should be able to advise us in good
time whenever any refugees leave Hongkong en route
to Shanghai. In addition it would greatly ease the
work of this office if the company's officers on
board steamers could arrange for the immigrants to
call at this office as soon after arrival as is con-
venient when their registration could be effected.

（批：To the / Ref / 1/7）
（印：RECEIVED BY / (S.B.) DIVISION / DATE 16 / 7 / 40 / [签名]）

档案号 5422 F
S. B. 162ation 7, Ho
日期 1940年7月3日。
主题 来自香港的中欧犹太人。
撰写人 副督察长 Pitts。转呈人 督察长 Crawford。

关于附上的印支轮船有限公司（Indo-China Steam Navigation Co. Ltd.）于1940年6月25日发出的关于欧洲难民从香港进入上海的函件，必须指出，根据自1940年7月1日起生效的修订规章，“……除非获得国际租界警方签发的入境许可证，否则不准入境……”
规章第(4)条规定，核实乘客在预订舱位前是否已获得警方签发的入境许可证的责任，由相关轮船代理承担。
鉴于这些规则，印支轮船有限公司的工作应大大简化，因为现在没有许可证的难民无法在此登陆。
由于本办公室对难民问题极为关注，且所有拟移民者必须持有许可证，轮船公司似乎应能在任何难民离开香港前往上海时及时通知我们。此外，如果轮船公司的工作人员能安排移民在抵达后尽快方便地来到本办公室进行登记，将极大减轻本办公室的工作负担。

（批注：To the / Ref / 1/7）
（印章：RECEIVED BY / (S.B.) DIVISION / DATE 16 / 7 / 40 / [签名]）

Confidential
P.20/1
PASSENGERS - ENEMY SUBJECTS
We acknowledge your letter of 13th instant and regret inconvenience caused by the Schuller party by s/s "Taisang" last trip.
As you are doubtless aware the local Government recently decreed that all Aliens were to quit the Colony and to assist our Authorities, we agreed to accept a limited number provided their Bona Fides were guaranteed.
The S.M.C. regulations of 22/10/39 were not overlooked but our Authorities who also are aware of these, assured us the requirements of the rules would be observed as regards any Aliens sent to your port.
The "Schuller" party are not Jewish, or in the strict sense Refugees, having business connections at Shanghai. They were permitted to remain here under local guarantees, after the outbreak of hostilities but with the tightening of restrictions the Authorities considered it expedient to deport such Aliens who are in a position to maintain themselves, or have relatives, at Shanghai. We can assure you the Authorities here are most particular in this regard, also in checking "Alien" baggage etc.
Incidentally we did not cancel any passages by s/s "Taisang" to accommodate the "Schuller" party as apparently stated by the Purser.
For your information a party of 8 Germans are travelling by s/s "Mingsang" sailing hence today. Particulars are as follows:-
Mr. & Mrs. H. Diestel & 2 Children. This family are in possession of G$500.00. Mr. Diestel is employed with the Comptoir Anglo-Continental Co., (a subsidiary of Sassoons) and is being transferred to your port.
Mrs. H.S. Nathan is the Mother-in-law of the Diestels.
Mr. & Mrs. A. Korczyn Possess G$800.00. Mr. Korczyn's brother resides in Shanghai.
Mrs. J. Wagner. A former Russian; German by marriage but now divorced. Previously resided in Shanghai now returning to live with her married daughter.
The Commissioner of Police here has telegraphed and written to his opposite number at Shanghai, fully explaining and we trust no difficulty will result.
We also attach letters from Messrs. Comptoir Contenental Ltd. as The Jewish Refugee Society which are self-explanatory.

乘客 - 敌国侨民
我方收到贵方本月13日来信，并对上次航程中由“泰山”轮（s/s "Taisang"）载运的舒勒（Schuller）一行造成的不便表示歉意。
想必贵方已知悉，当地政府最近颁布法令，要求所有外侨离境，为协助我方当局，我们同意接受有限数量的外侨，前提是其身份真实可靠得到保证。
我方并未忽视上海公共租界工部局1939年10月22日的规章，但我方当局也知晓这些规章，并向我们保证，送往贵港的任何外侨都将遵守规则要求。
“舒勒”一行并非犹太人，严格意义上也不是难民，他们在上海有商业联系。战事爆发后，他们曾在本地担保下获准留居此地，但随着限制收紧，当局认为将有能力维持生计或在上海有亲属的外侨驱逐出境是权宜之计。我们可以向贵方保证，当局在此方面非常谨慎，包括检查“外侨”行李等。
顺便提及，正如大副所称，我方并未取消“泰山”轮的任何舱位以容纳“舒勒”一行。
供贵方参考，一行8名德国人正乘坐今日从此地启航的“明生”轮（s/s "Mingsang"）前往。详情如下：
H. Diestel 先生及夫人和2名子女。该家庭持有国币500元。Diestel 先生受雇于英法大陆银行（Comptoir Anglo-Continental Co.，沙逊洋行的子公司），正被调往贵港。
H.S. Nathan 夫人是 Diestel 夫妇的岳母。
A. Korczyn 先生及夫人持有国币800元。Korczyn 先生的兄弟居住在上海。
J. Wagner 夫人。前俄罗斯人；因婚姻成为德国人，但现已离婚。此前居住在上海，现返回与已婚女儿同住。
此地警务处处长已致电并致函上海对口官员，充分说明情况，我们相信不会因此产生困难。
另附上英法大陆银行有限公司及犹太难民协会的信函，内容不言自明。

As a result of information secured in Shanghai
to the effect that the Hongkong Police were recently
expelling from the Colony certain undesirable
aliens, among whom might have been a number of
German Jewish refugees, enquiries were made at the
offices of Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co. Ltd. to
ascertain whether any of their ships had brought to
Shanghai any such persons.

An affirmative answer was received but details
as to whether the persons expelled and brought here
in the s.s. "Taisang" on June 10, 1940 were Jews
or Aryans were lacking. It was learned that four
Germans, Mr. O.R.F. MULLER, Mr. A. SCHULLER, Mrs. A.
SCHULLER and Mr. H. SCHULLER were forcibly placed on
board the steamer by the Hongkong Police and their
passages paid to Shanghai by the Hongkong Government.
They are at present residing at the Park Hotel, but
from their names it is not possible to state whether
they are Jews or not.

In order to prevent future occurrences of this
nature and in order to permit the Police in Shanghai
to exercise some control over these entries, it was
suggested to the local shipping office that they
make arrangements with their Hongkong branch to
inform the Shanghai office if and when the Hongkong
Police expelled further Germans without their being
in possession of the necessary landing-permits to
enter Shanghai. As a result, the letter dated
June 13, copy of which is attached, was despatched

根据在上海获得的情报，称香港警方最近正将某些不受欢迎的外国人驱逐出该殖民地，其中可能包括一些德籍犹太难民，因此向怡和洋行有限公司（Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co. Ltd.）办事处进行了查询，以查明其所属船只是否曾将此类人员载至上海。

得到了肯定的答复，但关于1940年6月10日由“泰山”轮（s.s. "Taisang"）驱逐并载抵此处的人员究竟是犹太人还是雅利安人，缺乏细节。获悉四名德国人，即 O.R.F. 穆勒（MULLER）先生、A. 舒勒（SCHULLER）先生、A. 舒勒夫人和 H. 舒勒先生，被香港警方强制送上轮船，其前往上海的船票费用由香港政府支付。他们目前居住在国际饭店（Park Hotel），但从他们的姓名无法判断他们是否为犹太人。

为了防止今后发生此类事件，并使上海警方能够对这些入境人员行使一定的控制权，已向当地航运办事处建议，与其香港分行做出安排，若香港警方再次驱逐没有进入上海所需登陆许可证的德国人，应通知上海办事处。据此，已发出日期为6月13日的信函，副本附后

the following German passengers from Hongkong:

Mr. O.R.F. Muller
Mr. A. Schuller
Mrs. A. Schuller
Mr. H. Schuller.

The Shanghai Municipal Police have now queried our
carriage of these passengers in view of the regulations in
force against the admission of refugees from Europe into
Shanghai, which regulations were passed on to you in our
letter of 26/12/39. We have explained to them that as we
are informed by the Purser these passages were arranged by
the Hongkong Government, other passengers having to be
cancelled to accommodate them and that they were escorted
on board by the Police.

The Police here fully appreciate that you had very
little option in the matter but are still worried over the
fact that the lack of any inspection of landing here deprives
them of any opportunity of checking up whether such passengers
are undesirable or otherwise. We have suggested that any
action to prevent the carriage of such passengers rather lies
out of our hands and could only be taken officially. They
have promised to look into the matter and see whether they
can make any effective communication to the Hongkong Government.

It would be of considerable assistance to them,
however, if they could have advance information of any similar
passengers coming up by our steamers, and we suggest that in
order to avoid further queries and possible complications you
might include in your despatch wire to us brief mention of so
many Germans or so many Italians.

JARDINE, MATHESON & CO., LTD.

General Managers, Indo-China S. N. Co., Ltd.

c.c. Shanghai Municipal Police
KdeCL/NC.

致怡和洋行有限公司，
总经理，
印度支那轮船航行有限公司，
香港。

乘客——敌国侨民。

于6月10日抵达此处的“泰山”轮（s/s "TAISANG"）从香港载来了以下德国乘客：

O.R.F. 穆勒（Muller）先生
A. 舒勒（Schuller）先生
A. 舒勒夫人
H. 舒勒先生。

鉴于现行禁止欧洲难民进入上海的法规（该法规已在我方1939年12月26日的信函中转达给贵方），上海公共租界工部局警务处现已对我方承运这些乘客提出质询。我们已向他们解释，据大副告知，这些行程是由香港政府安排的，为此不得不取消其他乘客的行程以容纳他们，且他们是由警方护送登船的。

此地的警方充分理解贵方在此事上几乎没有选择余地，但仍对因缺乏对此类人员登陆的检查，导致他们没有任何机会核查这些乘客是否属于不受欢迎分子或其他情况而感到担忧。我们已建议，任何防止承运此类乘客的行动而非我方力所能及，只能由官方采取。他们已承诺调查此事，并看看能否与香港政府进行任何有效的沟通。

然而，如果他们能提前获知有任何类似乘客将由我方轮船载来，将对他们大有裨益，因此我们建议，为了避免进一步的质询和可能的复杂情况，贵方在发给我们的发货电报中，可简要提及有多少名德国人或多少名意大利人。
